Full reports are in this folder: U1-harvester.md, U2-taxonomy.md, U3-data-assets.md, U4-wiki-code.md, U5-forrt.md, U6-landscape.md, U7-discovery.md (plus U3-docx-vs-fred-fuzzy.csv). Read the full report whenever a decision depends on details.

## U2-taxonomy (report only; structured return lost to a usage cutoff)
Summary: 17 LLM-taxonomy iterations (Dec 2025) never converged because the metric was two-LLM agreement (no human gold set, no kappa), n=100 seed-42 overfitting, single-label forcing on inputs that underdetermine the answer, and data skew (anchoring multi-site rows). Best stable facets: outcome format (5 values, 88-94% agreement), IV kind (3), effect type (4), broad domain (3-5, 92-97%). OpenAlex topics/subfields cover ~97% of rows and solve browse-by-area without inference (curated override table needed for odd subfield names; ignore legacy 'concepts'). Salvageable: the 362 hand-curated famous effects (docx_parsed_entries.json), canonical_effect_names.json (same list), all_known_effects.txt (598 names = legacy FReD 'effect' column 390 + docx 353, overlap only 149), openalex_original_enrichment.json + openalex_analysis/work_groupings.csv (1,599 works with topics), map_broad_category() 10-rule collapse, Cognitive Atlas term list (2,339 terms) for a paradigm facet. Current FReD v2 has NO effect-name column (only effect_id counter + description + discipline + tags); legacy v1 had 'effect' (440 unique). Recommendation: facets not a tree; observed metadata before inferred labels; every inferred label carries provenance + review state; similarity via embeddings, not fixed clusters. SECURITY: 51 scripts + CATEGORIZATION_IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md contain a live OpenRouter key and an OpenAI project key in plaintext; never copy into the new repo.

## U1-harvester
(full report: C:\Users\OMISTAJA\PsychologyReplication\_planning\understanding\U1-harvester.md)

**Summary:** The FReD-expansion harvester (harvest_crossref_replications.py + ~15 helper scripts) was a single-session effort on 2026-01-04 that searched Crossref with title phrases ("preregistered replication", "conceptual replication", "direct replication", "registered replication report", ...) scoped to an ISSN whitelist derived from legacy-FReD BibTeX, optionally gated by an OpenAlex psychology concept score >= 0.30, then applied a substring heuristic classifier. Only two runs completed (5 global queries capped at 200 results each, and 80 ISSNs x 6 phrases = 481 jobs); the "expanded" run died after job 1 (0 rows) and the "comprehensive" run (3,157 jobs) crashed at 12.8% with a Windows PermissionError because run_all_searches.py relaunched a second process on the same state file. The final artefact output/final_2021_psychology_replications.csv has 125 rows; my title/abstract review finds ~86 (69%) genuine empirical replication attempts (Crossref-filtered source 84% precise, free-text "simple search" source 41%), with 39 essays/meta-science pieces, supplemental-material/corrigendum DOIs and bio/medical false positives. 24/125 DOIs (19.2%) are already in current FLoRA doi_r (all of them real replications per FLoRA outcomes), 1 in doi_o; the docs' "124 new" was measured against the legacy FReD only. Against FLoRA ground truth the harvester's recall for 2021 is 24/140 = 17.1%, and the title-phrase primitive is structurally capped: only 64.9% of all 1,865 FLoRA replication papers have "replicat" in the title and only 33.9% pass the harvester's classifier title-only; the NON_PSYCH substring list ("rna" in "internalizing", "gene" in "general", "cell" in "excellence") would wrongly reject 151 (8.1%) genuine FLoRA titles. The replication_success (80 unclear/1 mixed/44 NaN) and original_study (regex tails) columns are useless, and no doi_o was ever resolved, so nothing is FLoRA-ingestible without manual work. All headline claims in README/PROJECT_STATUS/START_HERE ("94% precision", "1,500-2,000 papers expected", "foundation solid") have no measurement behind them; ENRICHMENT_COVERAGE_README.md is the one document with real numbers (abstract coverage 87% via PubMed>Crossref>OpenAlex>S2, OpenAlex hit 98.3%, OSF Replication Recipe schema). Worth porting: openalex_utils.normalize_doi, cursor+checkpoint pattern (one state per process), backoff helpers, OpenAlex abstract reconstruction, the phrase/meta/non-article keyword lists rewritten as word-boundary regexes, the multi-source abstract cascade and citation-graph collectors, and the ISSN-frequency prior computed from current FLoRA. Fundamentally wrong: paper-level "is it a replication" instead of (doi_o, doi_r, outcome) pairs, title search instead of citation-graph/abstract/venue-native discovery, no evaluation loop against the labelled FLoRA set that was sitting on disk, and a query plan (phrases x ISSNs x years ~44k jobs) that could never finish.

**Ideas:**
- Make the discovery unit the FLoRA triple (doi_o, doi_r, outcome, outcome_quote): every candidate must resolve the original study DOI (via Crossref `reference` list / OpenAlex referenced_works matched against 'Author et al. (YYYY)' in title/abstract) before it enters the review queue
- Citation-graph discovery as the primary primitive: for every FLoRA doi_o (and the 362 hand-curated famous effects), pull OpenAlex works that cite it, score them with replication-language features on abstract (OpenAlex abstract_inverted_index) + venue prior + topic; this bypasses the 35% no-'replicat'-in-title blind spot and directly yields the (original, replication) pair
- Build an always-on evaluation harness first: recall against FLoRA doi_r by year, precision on a human-labelled sample (start with the 125-row 2021 file already judged ~69%), per-source and per-phrase yield tables; refuse any strategy change that is not measured
- Venue-native feeds instead of blind search: Registered Reports (Crossref/OSF Registries/PCI RR), Meta-Psychology, Collabra, AMPPS, JDM, Journal of Numerical Cognition, AIS Transactions on Replication Research, Journal of Applied Econometrics replication section, Critical Finance Review, Psych Science Accelerator, CREP, ManyBabies/ManyLabs/RRR OSF projects, Data Replicada — plus OSF registrations using the Brandt 2013 'Replication Recipe' schema (structured ES/CI/success fields item30-item37) which nobody has mined
- Reuse and extend FORRT's own OpenAlex-based source (FLoRA source='openalex' contributed 23/140 of 2021 papers; see data/raw/forrt/fred-data/pipelines_flora_prepare_flora.qmd) and design the output to be contributable back in FLoRA's column conventions
- Replace substring heuristics with an LLM classifier over title+full abstract that outputs a structured record (is_replication_attempt, replication_type direct/conceptual/reproduction, original_citation string, outcome with quote, discipline) — the old keyword lists become few-shot guidance, not rules; keep word-boundary regex pre-filters only for obvious bio/CS noise
- Use OpenAlex `topics` (field=Psychology / subfield list) rather than deprecated `concepts`; use OpenAlex `search`/abstract.search and Crossref only as a secondary DOI-metadata source (its abstract coverage is ~36-57%)
- Query plan: one deep-paged query per phrase per year (Crossref query.title or OpenAlex search), post-filtered by venue prior and topic; a whole year should take minutes, not hours; one state file per process, real UTF-8 logging
- Exclude non-article DOIs up front (Crossref subtype, `update-to`, APA `.supp` suffix, 'Supplemental Material for', corrigenda, responses, commentaries) and route essays about replication to a separate 'meta-science' collection for the wiki rather than discarding them
- For the wiki: the 24 harvester finds that FORRT later added show FORRT's lag is ~months; a 'candidates awaiting FORRT' page with the review queue, plus per-paper abstract cascade and OpenAlex citation counts, gives users something FORRT does not have
- Guessing-game material: the human-reviewed queue (confirmed pairs with outcome quotes) doubles as high-quality game items; log reviewer decisions as labelled training data for the classifier

## U3-data-assets
(full report: C:\Users\OMISTAJA\PsychologyReplication\_planning\understanding\U3-data-assets.md)

**Summary:** Inventoried every csv/json/xlsx/txt/zip/docx/html data file in the project root, output/, cogatlas/ and openalex_analysis/ (about 130 files), verifying structure, row counts, columns and provenance with pandas/ijson. The most consequential finding is that the legacy FReD snapshot (root fred_database_english.csv, 4,376 x 100, column-identical to data/raw/forrt/osf/version-history/FReD_2.4.1_2025-06-25.xlsx sheet Data) is richer than the current output_FReD.xlsx (2,164 x 56): it covers 1,678 unique original DOIs vs 786, and carries effect names, ten closeness_* codings, power, CI bounds, preregistration/osf links, result/outcome codes, validation and notes that the current file dropped; the two link via legacy id == current fred_id (645 matches) and by DOI. docx_parsed_entries.json (362 effects) is a parse of FORRT's public Replications & Reversals list (the 2.4.1 workbook has a 583-row "Reversals Effects" sheet; 218 names match exactly) but uniquely adds per-effect status, prose critiques, Google-Scholar citation counts and free-text effect sizes; it has zero DOIs, so linking must go through the 329 quoted original titles (68% fuzzy-match to FLoRA/FReD/legacy refs; Crossref bibliographic lookup should resolve nearly all), not effect names (strict name match vs current FReD tags is 0%). A citation network exists for the 1,688 legacy DOIs (citation_dois.json: complete reference lists, citing DOIs capped at 600 without years; citation_data.json: rich citer metadata for only 200 DOIs) plus a 1,596-DOI full OpenAlex work dump (openalex_original_enrichment_full.json, incl. counts_by_year, topics, authorships) and 1,420 abstracts; these can power most-cited-unreplicated-effects and citation-trajectory features now, while citer-level after-failure timelines need a re-fetch. Third-party raw data (RP:P rpp_data, Many Labs 4, ManyBabies MB1) and Crossref harvest candidate pools (1,130 + 1,024 + 125 rows, only 24-33 already in FLoRA) are present and re-downloadable. Both .zip files are not zips (an OSF error JSON and an R ingest script), three csvs are 404 stubs, fred_database_english.json is invalid JSON, and 47 scripts embed a live OpenRouter API key that must be rotated. The ~60 taxonomy/clustering JSONs and the openalex_analysis crosstabs are regenerable experiment residue and should be archived. Full table and notes are in _planning/understanding/U3-data-assets.md, with per-entry fuzzy scores in U3-docx-vs-fred-fuzzy.csv.

## U4-wiki-code
(full report: C:\Users\OMISTAJA\PsychologyReplication\_planning\understanding\U4-wiki-code.md)

**Summary:** The wiki/ folder is a two-day (Aug 11-13 2026) Astro 7 + Preact MVP: a handsome "museum / field guide" skin over an almost empty data model. Of 6,006 built pages, 6,004 are placeholders (paper/attempt pages showing only title/authors/journal/year plus a "Metrics Pending" box, and three "Data Pending" collections); the only real content is one hand-written family page (literary fiction -> theory of mind) and a working Fuse.js search over 2,521 FLoRA rows. The pipeline reads FLoRA only, drops the outcome/type/quote columns, and never got FReD (the downloaded fred_effect.xlsx is a 1x1 sheet; the "codebook pdf" is actually an xlsx). Code is competent-but-sloppy Astro with real bugs: `--spacing-*` and `--color-ink-light/faint` CSS variables used but never defined (visible layout collapse), mono font never loaded, duplicate dead route files, nav links to non-existent pages, 1.72 MB explore.html because the entire index is inlined as island props, 186 duplicate ids, stale tests, starter README. The visual identity (warm paper #f7f6f2, ink #1a1a1a, vermilion #d83e27, ultramarine #1b2663, Inter headings + Playfair body, placard/timeline/badge components) grades B- as a mood board and D+ as an implemented system; keep the palette and tone, rewrite the CSS, change the body face, add outcome and chart palettes. The "Replication Family + three lenses" (author reports / numerical record / design differences) is the strongest idea on disk and maps directly onto FLoRA outcome+quote, FReD effect sizes/CIs, FReD closeness_* columns and the R package's seven success criteria; keep it at the centre but make it data-driven with curated overlays instead of hand-written prose. Recommendation: keep Astro (with Preact or Svelte islands), rebuild everything from a typed normalized-data layer, use content-collection loaders, Pagefind/MiniSearch pre-built indexes, build-time SVG charts, a single island for the game, and Cloudflare Pages (or GH Pages with `base`). Throw away all pages, normalize script, schema, dist, tests and boilerplate; reuse only the provenance-snapshot pattern, design tokens, the curated family JSON as an overlay template, and disciplines.json.

## U5-forrt
(full report: C:\Users\OMISTAJA\PsychologyReplication\_planning\understanding\U5-forrt.md)

**Summary:** FORRT publishes two datasets at different grains: FReD (effect-level, output_FReD.xlsx, 2,164 rows x 56 cols, with effect sizes/Ns/p-values and a narrative reported_success) and FLoRA (paper-level, output_flora.csv, 2,815 rows x 35 cols = 2,526 replications + 289 reproductions, outcome only, growing ~4 releases/week). The current public FReD.xlsx is row-for-row identical to fred-data/archive/2025-11-30_COSdata_validated.xlsx, which additionally carries precomputed Pearson r (r_o/r_r), statistical_success, PDF filenames and correct entry_id/effect_id (output_FReD.xlsx has entry_id==1 for every row, a pipeline bug). The legacy crowdsourced FReD 2.4.1 (4,661 x 100) is NOT superseded: only 1,548 current rows match it by DOI pair while 3,234 legacy rows are absent from the current file, and legacy alone carries effect names (443 + a 583-row Reversals Effects sheet), closeness_* (Brandt recipe), power, CIs, osf_link, prereg and project source labels (ML1/ML2/ML3/OSC2015/RRR*/OpAQ/CORE...). FReD joins to FLoRA by (doi_o, doi_r) for 1,783 rows / 678 pairs (2,036 rows with url_r and alt_identifier_r fallbacks) with 93.3% outcome agreement; 1,843 FLoRA replication pairs have no effect-size coding at all. Forest-plot-ready FReD rows: 1,163 with numeric ES on both sides (1,154 with Ns); applying the R package's conversion rules gives Pearson r for both sides in 1,061 rows (1,056 with Ns). FLoRA replication outcomes: 41.3% successful, 35.7% failed, 22.3% mixed; reproductions are 98% outcome-NA; only 9 non-English originals and 4 non-English replications. The FReD R package defines 7 success criteria on r (significance_r, significance_agg, consistency_ci, consistency_pi, homogeneity, homogeneity_significance, small_telescopes) plus LeBel-style signal/consistency coding and conversions d/r2/OR/eta2/f/f2/t/F(1,df)/z/chi2(1) -> r. FORRT's existing tools (Shiny Explorer v0.4.6 with tracker/scatter/z-curve/forest/correlates/moderators/reference checker; web Annotator; Zotero plugin + DOI/hash API at rep-api.forrt.org/v1) are paper/DOI-centric with no effect families, no topic pages and no guessing game; FORRT's OSF sub-datasets even include a saved copy of the 80,000 Hours 'guess which replicated' quiz. License CC-BY 4.0 (data) / MIT (code); citation string is in output_citation.txt. Full data dictionary and findings are in the report file.

**Key facts:**
- output_FReD.xlsx: 2,164 rows x 56 cols; 786 distinct doi_o, 320 distinct doi_r (+383 url_r), 1,116 fred_id, 859 (doi_o,doi_r) pairs, 1,003 entries by (ref_o,study_o,ref_r,study_r); entry_id is 1 on every row (bug: first(row_number()) in group); effect_id = row number
- reported_success in FReD: successful 985, failed 787, mixed 359, statistically successful but flawed 18, descriptive only 10, uninformative 5
- FReD discipline: 40 raw labels (34 after lower/strip): Social Psychology 643, Cognitive Psychology 439, Marketing 129, Psychology 109(+42 lowercase), Economics 104(+15), Management 100, Experimental Philosophy 75, Differential Psychology 69, Education 62, JDM 48, Linguistics 47, Neuroscience 43 ...
- FReD es_type_o: test statistic 758, d 320, etasq (partial) 173, r 162, beta (std) 151, b (unstd) 123, etasq 120, OR 74, r-squared 42; es_type_r: d 510, test statistic 485, r 210, etasq (partial) 198, beta (std) 149, b (unstd) 136, etasq 103
- FReD numeric es_value_o & es_value_r both: 1,163 rows (1,154 with n_o & n_r); converted-to-r both sides via R-package rules: 1,061 (1,056 with Ns): failed 448, successful 442, mixed 159; archive file precomputed r_o&r_r both: 733
- fred-data/archive/2025-11-30_COSdata_validated.xlsx = same 2,164 rows/order as output_FReD.xlsx (100% doi_o and es_value_o match) + r_o (839), r_r (1,002), statistical_success (446 TRUE/455 FALSE), file_o/file_r, fred_id_old, cos_phase1 (132 TRUE), correct entry_id (1,004 distinct) and within-entry effect_id
- Legacy FReD_2.4.1_2025-06-25.xlsx 'Data' = 4,661 x 100 (2 description rows -> 4,659 data rows), identical to osf/sub-datasets/FReD_legacy_v1.xlsx; validated: 1=1140, 0=1742, 3=693, 2=78, NA 1006; source: FORRT 1229, OpAQ 479, Individual submissions 515, ML1 352, Anna Van 't Veer 351, CORE 223, Boyce_etal2023 176, OSC 2015 167, ML3 145, AI search 113, OSF Registries 97, Soto 74, openmkt 50, XPHI 40, ML2 33, RRR1 29, RRR10 25, RRR9 23, RRR2 23, SSRP 21, datareplicada 19

- 7 success criteria (replication_outcomes.R) on Pearson r: significance_r (p_r<.05 & same sign; 'OS not significant' if p_o>=.05), significance_agg (FE meta ci_lb>0 & est>0), consistency_ci (es_o inside Fisher-z 95% CI of es_r), consistency_pi (es_r inside PI with SE=sqrt(1/(n_o-3)+1/(n_r-3))), homogeneity (Q-test p>=.05), homogeneity_significance (Q p>.05 & ci_lb>0, OS n.s. flagged), small_telescopes (es_r >= r giving 33% power at n_o)
- Conversions to r (effect_size_transformations.R): d,g -> d/sqrt(d^2+4); OR -> d=ln(OR)*sqrt(3)/pi; eta2 -> d=2*sqrt(eta2/(1-eta2)); f -> d=2f; f2 -> r=sqrt(f2/(1+f2)); r2 -> sqrt; test statistics t(df)=v, F(1,df2)=v, z=v,N=n, x2(1,N=n)=v; NA for beta/b/partial eta2/cramer's V/dz/cohen's h/semipartial r

## U6-landscape
(full report: C:\Users\OMISTAJA\PsychologyReplication\_planning\understanding\U6-landscape.md)

**Summary:** Researched the full landscape of replication trackers, wikis, forecasting projects, quizzes and adjacent data services via web search/fetch on 2026-09-07 and wrote the findings to U6-landscape.md. The only live, open, structured competitor is FORRT itself (FReD effect-level with stats, FLoRA paper-pair level without stats, plus Explorer/Annotator Shiny apps, a static per-DOI Replication Atlas claiming 4,700+ paired findings, a Zotero DOI-hash checker, R package, CC-BY data); it is row/paper-centric, has no effect identity, no narrative synthesis, no timelines, no forecasts, no game, and its authors document inconsistent outcome coding and collapsed free-text descriptions. ReplicationWiki (econ, ~4,484 studies/652 replications in 2020) returned HTTP 500 today and its founders reported outside contributions were "very limited"; Curate Science is a funding-seeking zombie whose data survives only as a 2022 web-archive snapshot inside FReD; PsychFileDrawer is unreachable (dead). OpenMKT (45 marketing replications, 11% success) and Replicability-Index (z-curve, journal rankings, textbook audits) are alive one-person efforts without APIs. DARPA SCORE concluded in Nature 2026: 49% replication, >50% effect-size shrinkage, repliCATS 76% and Replication Markets 78% accuracy, ML methods inconsistent; pooled forecasting literature shows markets 73%, surveys 66%, laypeople 59% (67% with Bayes factors), ML 70%, with p<=.005 originals replicating 74% vs 28% and interactions 20% vs main effects 53%. All existing "did it replicate" quizzes (80,000 Hours, ClearerThinking, Domke) are frozen 21-item SSRP-2018 sets with binary answers; users asked for probabilistic/calibration scoring. Retraction Watch (CC-BY CSV, daily, Crossref API) and Semantic Scholar citation contexts (free, though intents are mostly empty) are usable open inputs; Scite is closed. Transparent Replications (14 reports, 83% of recent top-journal studies replicated vs 55% forecast) plus Metaculus is the only live forecast-then-replicate loop. Textbook audits (Ferguson & Brown 2025; Schimmack series) exist only as papers, never as a structured per-effect table.

**Key facts:**
- FORRT Replication Atlas (https://forrt.org/flora-replication-atlas/) claims 4,700+ original findings paired with outcomes; per-DOI static pages with outcome quote, APA/BibTeX, OA and PubPeer links; no download/API on page
- FReD JOPD paper (doi 10.5334/jopd.101, Oct-2023 snapshot): 1,239 entries, 336 original studies, 468 replication findings; outcomes success 447 / informative failure 641 / inconclusive 15 / practical failure 3 / n.a. 133; sources: OSC2015 167 ES, ML1+ML3 497, RRRs 120, CORE 109, OSF Registries 95, individual 247, CurateScience (web archive Jan 2022); CC-BY 4.0; OSF 9r62x
- FORRT newsletters Feb/Apr 2026: FReD >1,000 findings, FLoRA >2,000 pairs, new ARIADNE/Explorer/Annotator, validator call, Replication Hub Showcase 1 July 2026
- ReplicationWiki: 2,600+ studies/339 replications (D-Lib Mar 2017), 4,484 studies/652 replications/231 journals/6.6M views (RePEc blog Aug 2020); MediaWiki; main page HTTP 500 on 2026-09-07; 'contributions from outside our team very limited'
- Curate Science homepage: Replication Tracker 'alpha' linking archived code (github ScienceCommons/curate_science); 'currently seeking new funding' (Dec 2022); solely Etienne LeBel
- PsychFileDrawer.org: DNS timeout on 2026-09-07 (both bare and www); domain expiry listed 2020-09-26 by index sites
- OpenMKT tracker: 45 direct preregistered replications, 5 successful (~11%); success = significant same direction + no obvious confounds; latest entry 2024; dataset downloadable at https://openmkt.org/blog/frm_display/replications-full/
- SCORE (cos.io/score; OSF osf.io/dtzx4): 3,900 claims, 865 collaborators; Nature 2026 papers Tyner et al. 10.1038/s41586-025-10078-y (replication 49% of 164; median ES shrinkage >50%), Aczel et al. 10.1038/s41586-025-09844-9 (robustness: 34% within 0.05 d, 74% same conclusion), Miske et al. 10.1038/s41586-026-10203-5 (reproducibility 54% precise/74% approx of 143; only 24% of 600 papers had data); repliCATS 76% and Replication Markets 78% accuracy; 3 ML methods not consistently effective
- Replication Markets: 3,000 claims from 62 journals, 10 rounds; 16 Nov 2021: 121 resolutions (79 regular+30 covid+12 meta), $142,623 prizes to 258 winners; replicationmarkets.com HTTP 522 today
- Gordon et al. 2021 PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0248780: 103 findings, >15,000 forecasts; markets 73% (75/103), surveys 66% (68/103); r=0.58; realized 49% vs forecast 61-63%; p<=.005 -> 74% replicated vs 28% for p>.005; 90% of error reduction in first 69 trades
- Altmejd et al. 2019 PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0225826: RF 70% CV (AUC .77), 71% preregistered OOS (AUC .73); top features post-hoc power, p, ES; interactions replicated 8/41 vs main effects 48/90; discipline dummies, language, location, subject pool not predictive
- Hoogeveen, Sarafoglou & Wagenmakers 2020 AMPPS 10.1177/2515245920919667 (OSF wg9s3): 233 laypeople, 27 SSRP+ML2 findings; 59% description-only, 67% with Bayes factors; experts historically 58% (RPP), 67% (ML2), 86% (SSRP)
- repliCATS PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0274429: IDEA protocol, 3,000 SCORE claims; validation 84% accuracy, AUC 0.94
- Wikipedia Replication_crisis (205,844 chars wikitext): RPP 36% of 97 (JPSP 23%, JEP:LMC 48%, Psych Sci 38%; cognitive 50% vs social 25%), SSRP 62%, ML2 50%; named psych effects only social priming, ego depletion, Bem ESP, power posing, subliminal perception, dissonance, BWAS; sections explicitly call for tools to check 'how often studies have been repeated'
- Ferguson & Brown 2025 J Gen Psych 153(2):272-285 doi 10.1080/00221309.2025.2587151: 16 textbooks (2018) vs 18 (2023); errors still common, biased toward making findings look consistent; SPE and Milgram misrepresented
- Transparent Replications (replications.clearerthinking.org): 14 reports by 24 Mar 2026; first 12 = 83% replicated vs psychologists' 55% forecast; 3 star ratings (transparency, replicability, clarity); Metaculus project 1774
- Institute for Replication: 110 econ/poli-sci papers reproduced/replicated by 15 Jun 2026; 232+ discussion papers; Meta Database of robustness checks
- PSA (psysciacc.org/projects.html): 15 projects; replications PSA001 (11,570 pp, 41 countries), PSA002 (null), PSA004 (Gettier 1.86x), PSA006 (trolley personal force universal), PSA008/JTF1 in progress
- Retraction Watch via Crossref: ~43k RW + 14k Crossref = ~50k retractions; CSV at gitlab.com/crossref/retraction-watch-data, 20 columns incl. OriginalPaperDOI/RetractionNature/Reason, updated each working day, CC-BY 4.0; API filter update-type:retraction
- Semantic Scholar Graph API citations endpoint returns contexts (citation sentences) free, but intents field was empty for all 20 citations of 10.1126/science.aac4716 and for Bargh 1996 on 2026-09-07; intents limited to full-text papers
- Scite: 1.2B citation statements supporting/contrasting/mentioning; ~USD 20/month; API by application only; per-DOI report pages 403 to bots
- Existing quizzes: 80000hours.org/psychology-replication-quiz (10/15/21 SSRP items, binary + don't know, compare to experts; commenters 71-93%; want probabilistic answers), ClearerThinking 2018 (same 21 items, compares to scientists/markets/public), Domke 2021 (13 effects from 2014 Social Psychology RRR issue, 0-4 scale, mean 0.8/4, all 'hot' effects failed); no 'Replication Roulette' exists
- Many Labs 1: 13 effects, 36 samples, >6,000 pp, 10 replicated, imagined contact weak, flag priming & currency priming failed; ML2: 28 findings, 50%; FORRT lists ML1-5 at osf.io/wx7ck..osf.io/7a6rd
- PCI RR: launched 2021, 100+ PCI-RR-friendly journals, PCI overall ~1,051 recommended preprints (Mar 2026); site blocked by Anubis anti-bot for fetchers

## U7-discovery
(full report: C:\Users\OMISTAJA\PsychologyReplication\_planning\understanding\U7-discovery.md)

**Summary:** Investigated ten discovery routes for replication studies beyond FORRT with live API tests. OpenAlex is the primary engine: field-32 (Psychology) works with "replication" in the title number 4,188 for 2015-2026 (194/yr in 2015 rising to ~470-510/yr in 2025-26), 74% with abstracts; the `cites:` filter accepts 100 OR'd seed IDs per call and, tested on 50 FLoRA originals, returned 130 citing works with "replication" in the title (1,183 in title+abstract) of which 92 were not yet in FLoRA, and on Kidd & Castano it surfaced every known replication. OpenAlex now bills per call (meta.cost_usd ~0.001; $1/day free, 10x with free key, 100 rps max). Semantic Scholar citation contexts work (87/200 citing papers had contexts, 4 with explicit replication-outcome sentences such as "failed to be replicated (Panero et al., 2016)") and are best used for outcome evidence rather than volume. PsyArXiv via OSF API has 623 "replication" preprints; OSF Registrations has 5,466 title hits, and FORRT's own Replication Recipe scraper yielded 95 rows from 139 hand-listed links. Crossref adds little beyond DOI/relation/retraction metadata (the old harvester produced 166 rows for 2021 only). Scite and PubPeer are keyed/paid signals, not discovery sources. An LLM triage stage with a strict JSON schema costs about $2.25 (Sonnet 5, batch) to $5.63 (Opus 5, batch) per 1,000 candidates; a weekly incremental crawl with per-source cursor state files and DOI-pair dedup against a weekly FLoRA refresh is designed, and FORRT's datasubmission_template.xlsx columns and submission page are documented for contributing back.

**Ideas:**
- Seed-driven citation crawl: every wiki effect page gets an 'open candidates' tab fed by OpenAlex cites:{original} + replicat* title; humans accept/reject from the page itself
- Use Semantic Scholar third-party citation contexts ('failed to be replicated (Panero 2016)') as a 'what the literature says' panel and as a guessing-game hint layer
- Preprint lead-time feature: show PsyArXiv replications as 'in progress / preprint' status before journal publication, linked via OSF attributes.doi and Crossref relation
- Registered-replication tracker: OSF registrations with Replication Recipe template that have no post-completion registration or paper after 3 years = 'file drawer' candidates displayed on effect pages
- Retraction and PubPeer flags on original-study pages via OpenAlex is_retracted (2,198 psych works) and Crossref update-to
- Student/course replications (Expra, CREP) as a distinct evidence tier in the wiki, harvested from OSF registrations
- Weekly auto-generated 'new candidates' report artifact + reviewer queue; monthly export to FORRT template with submission log, closing the loop
- Store LLM triage outputs with model id/version so the whole discovery layer is reproducible and re-runnable when models improve


## U8-forrt-ecosystem (added after the design panel ran; designers did NOT see this)
(full report: C:/Users/OMISTAJA/PsychologyReplication/_planning/understanding/U8-forrt-ecosystem.md)

**Summary:** FORRT is an active, funded engineering org (50 repos, 10 pushed in the last 10 days). Live API: https://rep-api.forrt.org/v1/{dois, original-lookup, prefix-lookup, search} (4,722 DOIs). flora-replication-atlas (CC0, SolidJS, prerendered, 4,717 originals, JSON-LD, OG images, browse by outcome/decade/journal) ALREADY provides per-original-DOI 'has it been replicated?' pages; paper-centric pages would duplicate it, so link to it instead. flora-extractor is FORRT's discovery engine (OpenAlex snapshot scan, rule specs, two-LLM screen, resolution + outcome coding; measured screen sensitivity 98-100%, stage-3 80/100 correct); its outputs are PUBLIC: data/extracted.csv = 3,147 machine-extracted pairs (2,197 unique replication DOIs, only 19 already in FLoRA) plus ~3,300 set-aside rows (target_pending 2,329, cannot_be_determined 799) with NO standing human-review queue: a ready-made candidate queue for us. flora-validation (validation.forrt.org) is their human layer (1,818 imported, 239 validated, 34 validators, gamified): template for our review queue. fred-apps publishes explorer-data.json with all 7 success criteria precomputed per FReD row; flora-explorer publishes citation timelines, author-overlap, journal-to-discipline map. journalranking = journal-level tracker; replicatethis = nomination portal with unscored binary predictions. NO 'did it replicate' game exists anywhere at FORRT; effect identity, three lenses, calibrated game, settled forecasts, textbook overlay, effect-level leaderboards are all ABSENT. Licences: atlas CC0; fred-apps/chromium-extension/fred MIT; flora-explorer/journalranking CC-BY; flora-zotero AGPL (do not copy); flora-extractor/flora-validation/flora-backend/fred-data code have NO LICENSE file, so ask before copying code (data is CC-BY 4.0). Positioning: independent effect-level explorer on FORRT data, link every DOI to the atlas, ingest their candidate CSVs, contribute reviewed pairs back in entry-sheet format, offer a citation-graph harvester (their issue #150) and recall harness they lack. Biggest risk: drifting into a paper-centric dashboard.

**Live feeds:** raw.githubusercontent.com/forrtproject/FReD-data/main/output/{flora.csv, FReD.xlsx, ...}; rep-api.forrt.org/v1/*; forrt.org/fred-apps/data/{explorer-data.json, flora-data.json, retraction-watch.csv.gz}; forrt.org/flora-explorer/data/*.json; flora-validation data/validated_export.csv; flora-extractor data/*.csv; atlas sitemap.xml + /doi/<doi>/ JSON-LD.
